# ATM Electronic Journal Parser and GL Reconciliation

> Parses raw ATM electronic journal logs and reconciles transactions against general ledger statements.

Author: Muhammad Tanveer (Full-Stack AI Automation Engineer)
Contact: mtanveertahir66@gmail.com | https://www.linkedin.com/in/muhammad-tanveer-advenno/
Repository: https://github.com/haddindeve/ej-rolls-atm-reconciliation
Source availability: implementation held in a private repository; access on request.

## Summary
Reconciling ATM activity means reading electronic journal logs - unstructured, machine-specific text - and matching them by hand against general ledger entries. It is slow, and the errors it produces are financial ones.

A parser that turns raw EJ text into structured transaction records, then a reconciliation stage that matches those records against GL statements and reports what does not agree. The parser is tolerant of the format variation that makes these logs awkward to process.

## Stack
Language: Python, Parsing: Tolerant text parsing of EJ formats, Output: Structured reconciliation reports

## Capabilities
- Electronic journal parsing
- Format-variation tolerance
- Automated GL matching
- Discrepancy reporting

## Outcomes
- Manual log reading replaced by structured extraction
- Discrepancies surfaced as exceptions rather than found by inspection

## FAQ
Q: What is an ATM electronic journal?
A: The machine's own transaction log - a plain-text record of every operation, with format varying by machine and vendor.

Q: What does reconciliation produce?
A: A report of matched transactions and, more importantly, the exceptions that do not agree with the ledger.

Q: Why is parsing hard?
A: EJ output is unstructured and varies between machines, so the parser has to tolerate format differences.

Q: Is the code available?
A: Private repository; access on request.
